Business.description: What the major business and general-news outlets are leading with.
Business.overview: Business coverage across outlets is dominated by mounting anxiety over AI-related debt and spending after a bruising tech selloff, alongside the US midterm elections' economic dimension — record gas prices, oil-market swings tied to Iran diplomacy, and what a possible Democratic sweep could mean for AI regulation and markets. A major AI hardware M&A deal and the fallout from the largest-ever crypto hack round out the shared business agenda.

stories.headline: Cracks widen in the AI borrowing binge as hyperscalers face scrutiny
stories.summary: NYT's DealBook reports that investors are growing increasingly concerned about the debt-fueled spending spree underpinning the AI buildout, a theme echoed across the business press this week.

stories.headline: S&P cuts Meta's outlook to negative as AI cash burn deepens
stories.summary: Fortune reports S&P Global revised Meta's outlook to "negative" from "stable," citing negative cash flow and uncertainty around its capital expenditure plans, with projected free cash flow staying negative through 2028, as OpenAI reportedly cut its fundraising target and Alphabet posted its worst trading day on record.

stories.headline: Marvell to buy Lumentum in $115bn all-stock AI connectivity bet
stories.summary: FT reports Silicon Valley's Marvell and data-centre component maker Lumentum struck an all-stock deal the companies said would create a leader in AI connectivity, a rare big-ticket M&A move amid the broader tech selloff.

stories.headline: Gas prices hit record highs under Trump on eve of midterms
stories.summary: FT reports average US fuel costs during Trump's second term have passed Biden-era levels as affordability concerns dominate Tuesday's midterm polls, a theme Washington Post also hammers with data showing regular gas is roughly 40 percent higher than a year ago in some battlegrounds.

stories.headline: Oil prices tumble as Trump signals more time for Iran diplomacy
stories.summary: Bloomberg reports oil sank after a report that Trump wants to give diplomacy with Iran more time before resuming strikes that could stymie a regional energy recovery, a move CNBC says is being watched closely alongside midterm trading.

stories.headline: Binance resumes withdrawals after record $6.3bn crypto hack
stories.summary: WSJ reports Binance resumed withdrawals after suffering its biggest-ever hack, saying it has replaced roughly 95 percent of the stolen assets so far; BBC adds the FBI has linked the breach to a North Korean group and that users withdrew $3.6bn following the incident.

stories.headline: Trump family-linked mining venture seeks $2 billion public listing
stories.summary: WSJ reports the firm set to become Kaz Resources has secured letters of interest for up to $1.6 billion in US funding as it aims to go public, drawing scrutiny from Sen. Elizabeth Warren.

stories.headline: Gulf economies strain under fallout from the Iran war
stories.summary: NYT reports that Gulf states like Saudi Arabia and the UAE, which had worked to diversify away from oil dependence, have seen growth plunge during a year of regional strife, complementing WSJ's report that Saudi Arabia's economy shrank 3.8 percent as oil output fell.

Business.gaps: The Information, Forbes, Puck, and Business Insider did not surface any relevant recent business coverage in available search results or feeds.

US politics.overview: US political outlets are almost entirely consumed by the eve of the 2026 midterms, with the biggest storyline being Rep. Haley Stevens' stunning last-minute endorsement of Republican Mike Rogers over her own party's Senate nominee in Michigan. Coverage also centers on final Cook Political Report ratings showing Democrats favored to retake the House, Sen. Chris Murphy's hospitalization after a stroke, and a wave of election-administration lawsuits in Alaska, California and elsewhere.

stories.headline: Haley Stevens endorses Republican Mike Rogers, stunning Michigan Democrats
stories.summary: After months backing the Democratic ticket, Rep. Haley Stevens endorsed GOP Senate candidate Mike Rogers over her former primary rival Abdul El-Sayed less than 48 hours before Election Day, saying El-Sayed's campaign had told her she was no longer welcome. The Michigan Democratic Party subsequently expelled her and Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer called the move a 'despicable betrayal.'

stories.headline: Cook Political Report: Democrats could win up to 240 House seats
stories.summary: With Republicans' narrow House majority appearing poised to flip, the Cook Political Report's final ratings favor Democrats in 220 seats with 17 true toss-ups, and separate reporting suggests Democrats could end up with their largest majority since 2009.

stories.headline: Sen. Chris Murphy hospitalized after stroke, 'awake and alert'
stories.summary: Connecticut Sen. Chris Murphy was hospitalized over the weekend after experiencing numbness in his arm; his office says he is responding well to treatment and expected to recover.

stories.headline: Judge tosses DOJ lawsuit seeking to delay Alaska vote certification
stories.summary: A federal judge rejected the Justice Department's lawsuit seeking to delay certification of Alaska's Senate race amid the 'Decoy Dan' controversy involving two candidates named Dan Sullivan, and the DOJ is now preparing to appeal.

stories.headline: Election lawsuits and ballot disputes pile up before Election Day
stories.summary: The Trump administration has pushed to set aside thousands of ballots in California and Washington over unproven noncitizen-voting claims, with a federal judge rejecting the California effort and election officials in both states pushing back, while North Carolina has flagged thousands of mail ballots for technical problems.

stories.headline: Poll flashes warning signs for Republicans in seven battleground Senate races
stories.summary: Fox News polling shows Democrats leading in Texas, Kansas, Ohio, Maine and Alaska Senate races, with Trump's approval at just 38% across the seven battlegrounds surveyed.

stories.headline: Trump to deliver closing midterm message at the Reflecting Pool
stories.summary: President Trump plans to make his final pitch to voters at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, using the Washington landmark to highlight his administration's beautification projects.

stories.headline: 'A lot of Republicans have held their tongues': Anger at Trump is growing
stories.summary: Politico reports that while few Republicans will publicly criticize President Trump over the party's rocky midterm prospects, many are far more blunt in private conversations.

US politics.gaps: NOTUS and SCOTUSblog had no recent relevant coverage found via search; Politico, NYT, WSJ and The Guardian were reported only from the feed items provided since they block web search.

Tech & AI.overview: Tech and AI outlets are converging on three major threads: the fallout from a massive North Korea-linked crypto heist and a wave of European retail cyberattacks, intensifying scrutiny of AI-fueled market froth (debt-financed data center spending, stock volatility, insurance against an AI bubble), and Anthropic's blockbuster IPO process gaining global momentum alongside a new Marvell-Lumentum mega-merger. Several outlets are also tracking how AI labs are simultaneously enabling and defending against a surge in AI-powered cyberattacks and deepfake abuse.

stories.headline: FBI blames North Korea for $6.3 billion Binance crypto heist
stories.summary: The FBI attributed the massive Binance breach to North Korean hackers under an operation it labeled 'TraderTraitor,' as the exchange began restoring withdrawals after covering most of the stolen assets.

stories.headline: Anthropic pushes IPO rollout into Japan with up to $3.5 billion share offer
stories.summary: Anthropic is seeking billions from Japanese investors as part of its landmark US IPO rollout, extending a global roadshow that already includes Australia, Canada and parts of Europe; the Claude maker filed its S-1 last month and is reportedly expected to receive a high 'junk' credit rating after listing.

stories.headline: Investors grow anxious over AI's debt-fueled buildout and market exposure
stories.summary: The New York Times, WSJ and FT are all flagging mounting investor unease about the debt-financed AI infrastructure spending spree, with WSJ reporting investors are racing to buy insurance against the AI trade and FT arguing rising interest rates threaten to puncture the AI bubble.

stories.headline: Marvell to buy Lumentum in $115 billion all-stock AI connectivity bet
stories.summary: Marvell agreed to acquire optical components maker Lumentum in one of the biggest tech M&A deals of the year, aiming to build an AI connectivity rival to Broadcom; both companies have previously received Nvidia investment.

stories.headline: Cyberattacks hit supermarket freezers across Belgium and Sweden
stories.summary: A new wave of suspected cyberattacks has struck grocery chains across Belgium and Sweden, causing sudden temperature spikes in fridges and freezers in a pattern that mirrors earlier incidents in France.

stories.headline: Wired exposes hundreds of apps hiding abusive AI deepfake tools
stories.summary: Wired's investigation found roughly 400 apps and websites tied to Chinese-language developers that appear to be ordinary AI tools but secretly let users generate violent and sexually abusive deepfake images and video, bypassing app store review.

stories.headline: OpenAI preps post-midterm Washington lobbying push and data center rebrand
stories.summary: OpenAI is gearing up for a political lobbying and PR offensive once the US midterms conclude, while separately TechCrunch reports the company may rebrand its unpopular data centers as 'AI compute campuses.'

stories.headline: AI labs race to profit from the hacking surge their own models enable
stories.summary: The Economist reports OpenAI and Anthropic see a major business opportunity in AI-driven cybersecurity even as their models fuel a rise in hacking; Anthropic itself announced a new 'Cyber Mission' initiative aimed at securing critical systems.

Tech & AI.gaps: The Verge, Wired, Ars Technica, NYT, WSJ, FT, The Economist, and The Guardian block direct web search, so coverage from those outlets reflects only the feed items supplied. No usable recent items were found for 404 Media, Google DeepMind, or OpenAI's own newsroom in this cycle.

Energy.overview: Coverage across energy and climate outlets is dominated by the sharp drop in oil prices as US-Iran diplomacy raises hopes of avoiding a wider Middle East conflict, alongside fallout from the Iran war on Gulf economies and global LNG buyers. Clean-energy-focused outlets (Heatmap, Canary Media, Carbon Brief, Latitude Media) are separately tracking data-center emissions growth, a drop in US clean energy jobs, the UN biodiversity summit outcomes, and energy politics ahead of the US midterms.

stories.headline: Oil Prices Tumble as Iran Diplomacy Eases Supply Fears
stories.summary: Oil prices dropped more than 4% after renewed US-Iran diplomatic efforts reduced fears of a supply disruption, reversing gains from the prior week.

stories.headline: U.S. Pushes to Restore Russian Gas Sales to Europe Via Ukraine
stories.summary: Washington is floating a plan to revive Russian gas flows to Europe through Ukraine as part of an energy ceasefire, though the idea faces pushback from European capitals.

stories.headline: Saudi Arabia's Economy Shrinks 3.8% as Oil Output Falls
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia's economy contracted as the Arab world's largest economy struggled to absorb the economic fallout of the Iran war and renewed tensions with Yemen's Houthis.

stories.headline: Cash-Strapped LNG Buyers Like Bangladesh Are at Breaking Point
stories.summary: Dependence on Qatari LNG has squeezed Bangladesh's textile manufacturers financially, putting export orders at risk to international competitors.

stories.headline: U.S. Data Centers Will Emit More Carbon Than All of Mexico
stories.summary: A new Sierra Club analysis finds fossil-fueled power plants built to run AI data centers are set to emit 460 million metric tons of CO2 by 2030, roughly matching Mexico's entire economy and erasing 15 years of U.S. power-sector emissions progress.

stories.headline: US Clean Energy Jobs Fell in 2025 for the First Time in Years
stories.summary: Canary Media reports clean energy employment dipped during Donald Trump's first year back in office, with many more projected jobs unlikely to materialize due to canceled clean energy projects.

stories.headline: COP17: Key Outcomes Agreed at the UN Biodiversity Conference in Yerevan
stories.summary: Carbon Brief reports countries completed the first global review of progress toward reversing nature loss by 2030 at the UN biodiversity summit in Yerevan.

stories.headline: The Most Pivotal Midterm Races for Energy
stories.summary: Latitude Media outlines which upcoming US midterm races will be most consequential as competing visions of energy affordability head to the ballot box.

Energy.gaps: No usable recent (last 24-48h) items could be found for E&E News or Argus Media via search; E&E's most recent indexed stories were from May 2026. Reuters, FT, and The Economist had no relevant energy/climate feed items provided and were not independently searchable within the allotted searches. Utility Dive's listed items were sponsored content and excluded from ranking.

China.description: China politics, economy and business coverage.
China.overview: Coverage across outlets converges on two deepening fronts: Beijing's post-plenum tightening of Communist Party discipline and surveillance over officials ahead of next year's leadership reshuffle, and escalating cross-strait friction with Taiwan over coast guard patrols and APEC treatment. Business and trade press are focused on China's EV and battery dominance, EU export-quota negotiations, record trade surpluses, and the fast-moving US-China AI/tech rivalry playing out in courtrooms and data centers.

stories.headline: CCP tightens surveillance and promotion rules for officials after fifth plenum
stories.summary: Following the fifth plenum, the party has overhauled cadre promotion rules to scrutinize officials' crisis experience and disciplinary records ahead of next year's leadership reshuffle, while a separate party document calls for closer monitoring of officials' assets and online activity and Nikkei reports a new big-data system to track members' online behavior for corruption.

stories.headline: Cross-strait tensions flare over Chinese coast guard patrols and APEC invitation snub
stories.summary: Taiwan's coast guard accused Chinese patrol vessels of harassing shipping off its east coast and rejected Beijing's claimed jurisdiction, while Taiwan's foreign minister separately protested that China, as APEC host, downgraded Taiwan's formal invitation to the Shenzhen summit as discriminatory treatment.

stories.headline: US export controls push Chinese AI firms toward Singapore-based data centers
stories.summary: Chinese AI companies have become the top customers of Singapore-based data-center operator DayOne as Washington's chip export curbs reroute compute demand through Asia, with the firm now also courting US investors; Rest of World separately reports Western startups are reworking open-weight Chinese AI models to strip censorship for Western clients.

stories.headline: Huawei trial in Brooklyn exposes company's internal workings
stories.summary: Proceedings in the federal case United States v Huawei Technologies, underway in a Brooklyn courthouse, are revealing previously hidden details of how the Chinese tech champion operates amid long-running US sanctions disputes.

stories.headline: Debate grows over what China's record trade surplus really signals
stories.summary: China's merchandise trade surplus is on track for another annual record after reaching nearly $940 billion in the first nine months of 2026, up 7.8% year-on-year, but Caixin's analysis argues this reflects manufacturing competitiveness rather than a dangerously unbalanced economy, noting the current-account surplus remains well below Germany, Japan and South Korea's levels.

stories.headline: Chinese automakers head to Beijing for talks on limited EU hybrid export quotas
stories.summary: Several Chinese automakers are reportedly meeting Beijing officials to compete for allocations under a constrained overall quota governing hybrid vehicle exports to the European Union.

stories.headline: Chinese firms extend dominance of global EV battery market
stories.summary: CATL and BYD led a group of seven Chinese companies that together held 73% of the global EV battery market in the first nine months of 2026, up 3.5 percentage points from a year earlier, with CATL alone commanding 39.1% share.

stories.headline: Apple to roll out Alibaba's Qwen AI model for iPhones in China starting Nov. 4
stories.summary: Apple confirmed it will begin beta testing Apple Intelligence in mainland China on November 4, integrating Alibaba's Qwen model into Siri, Writing Tools and Visual Intelligence via an iOS developer beta.

China.gaps: No recent (last 48h) items could be found or surfaced via search for Sixth Tone, China Media Project, Yicai Global, CGTN, China Daily or Xinhua; Global Times search results returned only older Japan/Taiwan diplomacy pieces outside the 48-hour window. Reuters, AP, FT, NYT and The Economist block search and had no relevant feed items provided this cycle.

Gulf & Middle East.overview: Coverage across Gulf and Middle East outlets is dominated by the fallout from the Qatar LNG tanker attack and the parallel US-Iran diplomatic push in Doha ahead of the November 3 US midterms, alongside Israel's ongoing Hebron siege and Gaza strikes. Business-focused outlets (AGBI, Zawya, Arabian Business) are tracking the economic toll of the eight-month war, from GCC growth downgrades to rising living costs.

stories.headline: Qatar LNG tanker Al Mayeda struck in Gulf, sparking regional condemnation
stories.summary: Qatar's LNG carrier Al Mayeda was hit by unidentified objects while sailing in the Gulf on Friday evening, with Doha calling it a dangerous act threatening maritime navigation and global energy supplies and warning it reserves the right to take necessary measures. Saudi Arabia separately condemned the attack and called for urgent international action to protect shipping and global energy supplies.

stories.headline: Iranian negotiators hold third day of Doha talks to avert renewed war
stories.summary: Iranian negotiators were in Doha for a third straight day of talks with Qatari mediators aimed at ending the US-Israeli war, with the discussions coordinated in regular contact with Washington amid fears the conflict could reignite after the November 3 US midterms. Iran's Supreme Leader ordered the armed forces to be prepared for renewed strikes even as both sides signaled some diplomatic movement.

stories.headline: Hebron siege enters 10th day as Israel threatens wider West Bank offensive
stories.summary: Israeli forces maintained their lockdown of Hebron for a 10th day, with the city's mayor estimating daily economic losses exceeding $3.8 million and more than 3,300 Palestinians displaced or affected as homes were demolished and over 300 businesses closed. Israeli troops also arrested Palestinian teachers near Hebron and raided a UN-run school in East Jerusalem's Shufat camp on Sunday.

stories.headline: Israeli strikes kill at least eight in Gaza as ceasefire violence continues
stories.summary: Israeli strikes killed at least eight Palestinians, including five police officers, in two separate attacks on Gaza on Sunday, according to medics, part of continued violence despite the nominal ceasefire. Middle East Eye separately reported strikes killing nine people including a child the same day.

stories.headline: IMF projects GCC economy will contract 4.8% in 2026 on war disruption
stories.summary: The IMF's October Regional Economic Outlook sharply downgraded 2026 growth for the six GCC economies, projecting a 4.8% contraction this year followed by a 9.1% rebound in 2027 as the Middle East conflict disrupts hydrocarbon production, shipping and trade. Kuwait is seen facing the steepest contraction at 16.7%, followed by Qatar at 15.6% and Bahrain at 11.3%, while Oman is the only member expected to grow.

stories.headline: Gulf living costs climb even as headline inflation stays contained
stories.summary: AGBI reports that GCC inflation remains subdued overall despite the Iran war's impact on global energy and commodity prices, but food and transport costs are rising sharply, with Dubai's annual inflation hitting a four-year peak of 5.7% in June before easing to 5.03% in September. Analysts warn further consumer price increases are likely as regional conflict continues to heighten cost pressures.

stories.headline: Houthis renew threats against Saudi Aramco and aviation
stories.summary: Houthi media, citing an anonymous military official, repeated threats on Sunday against Saudi oil giant Aramco and aviation inside the kingdom, adding to regional tensions over maritime and energy security.

stories.headline: South Korea's Sinokor emerges as dominant player in Hormuz oil trade
stories.summary: A little-known South Korean shipping company, Sinokor, has come to control roughly half of all tanker transits through the Strait of Hormuz, having placed a large bet just before the Iran war began.

Gulf & Middle East.gaps: Could not find current, distinct coverage from Khaleej Times, Saudi Gazette, Al Arabiya English, Ynetnews or Haaretz beyond outdated cached pages; Reuters, AP, FT and BBC block search and had no relevant feed items provided.

Africa.description: Africa politics, economy and business coverage.
Africa.overview: Coverage across these outlets is dominated by the deepening Ebola outbreak in DR Congo, Horn of Africa conflict dynamics (Ethiopia-Eritrea tensions, Sudan-Ethiopia drone dispute, Tigray fighting), and major corporate/finance stories including Dangote's oversubscribed refinery IPO, Madagascar's multi-billion-dollar mining/energy fundraising push, and African fintech's troubled run at Wall Street listings.

stories.headline: Ebola death toll in DR Congo tops 5,372 as fatality rate passes 50%
stories.summary: The ongoing DRC Ebola outbreak has reached a case fatality rate above 50%, with the death toll climbing past 5,372; Africa Confidential separately reports that health ministers are meeting on a widening response as funding gaps persist and cases spread to new countries.

stories.headline: Dangote Refinery's $1.6bn IPO draws nearly triple demand
stories.summary: Africa Confidential reports that Nigerian investors placed about $4.78 billion in orders for Dangote Refinery's planned November listing, nearly tripling the offer size; African Business also flagged the oversubscribed IPO closing.

stories.headline: Sudan files UN complaint against Ethiopia over deadly drone strikes
stories.summary: Khartoum has lodged formal complaints with the UN accusing Ethiopia of a drone campaign it says has killed or wounded 484 civilians since February.

stories.headline: UN peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara ends after 35 years
stories.summary: The UN's long-running peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara has formally shut down after the Security Council failed to renew its mandate, a major shift in the decades-old territorial dispute.

stories.headline: Madagascar teams with Gemcorp to raise up to $5bn for energy and mining
stories.summary: Mining Weekly (via Bloomberg) reports Madagascar wants to raise as much as $5-billion by teaming up with asset manager Gemcorp Capital Management to fund energy, infrastructure and mining projects in the island nation.

stories.headline: OPay's abandoned Wall Street listing raises questions for African fintech
stories.summary: TechCabal examines the fallout after OPay's bankers abruptly abandoned what would have been a roughly $4 billion capital markets transaction, part of a broader TechCabal Daily report that OPay has withdrawn its US IPO.

stories.headline: MTN Nigeria profit jumps 55% but cash reserves shrink
stories.summary: MTN Nigeria's profit after tax rose 55.3% to ₦1.17 trillion in the first nine months of 2026, even as cash reserves fell nearly 40% due to dividends, network investment and debt costs.

Africa.gaps: The Continent had no coverage within the last 48 hours in available search results (only older weekly PDF issues were found). Reuters, AP, BBC, FT, NYT and WSJ block web search and no relevant Africa-focused feed items from them were provided, so their current coverage could not be assessed.

Media.overview: Media trade coverage over the past 48 hours is dominated by the U.S. midterm elections' effect on journalism and campaigns (the Haley Stevens endorsement fiasco, CBS's '60 Minutes' handling of a Michigan Senate race), alongside Netflix's UK layoffs, Meta's standoff with global publishers over AI scraping terms, and ongoing UK industry labor strife at the BBC.

stories.headline: Haley Stevens' Eleventh-Hour GOP Endorsement Sets Off Media Firestorm
stories.summary: Michigan Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens' surprise withdrawal of support for her party's Senate nominee and endorsement of Republican Mike Rogers on the eve of the midterms triggered intense coverage, including a widely-discussed CNN interview and a heckled press conference where she was called a "traitor."

stories.headline: Netflix Lays Off Up to 3% of London Staff, Production VP Anna Mallett Exits
stories.summary: Netflix is cutting up to 3% of its London headquarters staff, with production VP Anna Mallett among those departing, as the streamer's cost-cutting reaches its UK operation.

stories.headline: Meta Delays New Publisher Terms After Norwegian Court Blocks Them, Senator Pressure
stories.summary: Meta has pushed back implementation of controversial new ad and business terms that would allow broad scraping of publisher content for AI training, after a Norwegian court blocked the terms and a coalition of Norwegian news publishers sued, while a U.S. senator called the plan "a gross abuse of Meta's power."

stories.headline: BBC Journalists to Vote on Strike Over Compulsory Redundancy Threat
stories.summary: BBC staff will ballot on strike action between November 3-24 after the broadcaster said it could not guarantee avoiding compulsory redundancies as it cuts roughly 100 News jobs and 250 posts in its Nations division as part of £500m in savings.

stories.headline: Inside the '60 Minutes' Scramble Over El-Sayed Interview
stories.summary: Status reports that a CBS News correspondent's "ill-fated post" and internal reservations among producers nearly derailed a "60 Minutes" sit-down with Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed ahead of the broadcast's Sunday airing.

stories.headline: Russell Brand Defense Rests Case, Says Channel 4 Documentary "Poisoned Well of Justice"
stories.summary: In closing arguments, Russell Brand's defense lawyer argued a 2023 Channel 4 documentary about the comedian "poisoned the well of justice deliberately," while separately telling jurors there is "no evidence" he is a predator.

stories.headline: CTV Overtakes Cable in Political Ad Spend for First Time in a Midterm
stories.summary: Political advertisers have spent a record $11.4 billion this midterm cycle, with connected TV now taking in more than half of the new money and running nearly double cable's share, Adweek reports.

stories.headline: Journalism Job Cuts Tracker: People Inc. Cuts 195 Jobs, Telegraph to Cut Around 100
stories.summary: Press Gazette's running tally of 2026 media layoffs shows continued contraction across the industry, from People Inc. and the Telegraph to BBC News, Metro, Vox, Buzzfeed and the Associated Press.

Media.gaps: Puck's media vertical (In the Room) had no items published within the last 24-48 hours at time of search; its most recent media story was over a week old. NYT, WSJ, FT and The Guardian block web search, so only their provided feed items (one NYT piece on election coverage, one WSJ piece on Netflix viewing hours) could be reported.
